title: The Exodus Northward
question: Today, can the brother lead the women through the exodus?
light: summer sunlight from the east, deep black shadows
palette: dust white, brick brown, privet green, smoke black, flame orange

london_exodus.described: The river fills the picture from lower left to lower right, with jammed steamers, lighters, barges, warehouses, and a stone bridge across the middle distance. A dark tower stands at the left edge behind the wharves. Black vapour lies low between the arches and extends toward the far water. The city belongs to the wide view while faces remain distant. Summer sunlight falls from the east across the brown river and catches the bridge towers. Smoke haze softens the far skyline. The riverbank occupies the foreground, with ropes, wet stone, and mooring posts between the camera and the crowded water.
london_exodus.route: south-bank foreground to the stone bridge at the far water
london_exodus.geometry: The lower left holds the stone river bank; the lower right holds brown water and moored barges; the stone bridge spans the far edge at wide size; black vapour lies between the middle arches; the dark tower occupies the far-left quarter; warehouses line the right edge; steamers fill the water between foreground and bridge; the bridge towers rise above the traffic; the far bank closes the horizon beneath grey smoke.
london_exodus.crowd: the chapter's people press among the river craft and wharves
london_exodus.ambience: steamer whistles, ropes knocking, river wash, distant shouting

chalk_escape.described: Chalk Farm Road runs diagonally through the picture between the yellow-brick goods-yard wall at the left edge and the three-storey shop fronts at the right edge. Cast-iron gates and the round engine house sit along the left side. The cycle shop window occupies the near right edge with black bicycles behind broken glass. Haverstock Hill rises at the far end beneath hazy morning light. The brother's route crosses from the goods yard toward the shop terrace, then continues north toward Edgware. Morning sunlight falls from the east across the road and shop fronts. Glass shards and straw mark the pavement, while the road carries the pressure of fleeing traffic toward the hill.
chalk_escape.route: goods-yard gates to the cycle shop and northward road
chalk_escape.geometry: The left edge carries the high goods-yard wall and cast-iron gates; the right edge carries the shop terrace at medium size; the cycle shop window stands in the near right quarter; the road runs between the wall and shops to Haverstock Hill at the far edge; the engine house rises behind the wall; scattered glass occupies the lower pavement; the shop doorway sits beside the broken window; the hill road leaves the frame beyond the shops.
chalk_escape.crowd: many fugitives cross among vehicles and bicycles
chalk_escape.ambience: vehicle wheels, glass fragments, shouted directions, railway steam

grass_lane_rescue.described: The grass lane runs from the stile at the left edge around the old oak in the middle distance and toward the pony-chaise on the right-hand verge. Hawthorn hedges fill both side edges, with elder flowers and dog-roses above the grass. The chaise occupies medium size beneath the southern hedge; its red-lined seat and travelling bag remain visible. A field gate and red-brick farmhouse sit at the far right beyond the hedge. Morning sunlight falls from the east through the hedge tops, placing bright bands across the dusty ruts and grass verge. The bend hides the lane beyond the oak, while the verge gives the chaise room beside the hedge.
grass_lane_rescue.route: stile at the west edge to the chaise beneath the east hedge
grass_lane_rescue.geometry: The stile occupies the left edge at medium size; the dusty ruts run from the lower edge toward the oak at centre; the chaise rests on the right verge at medium size; the farmhouse and field gate sit at the far-right edge; hawthorn hedges frame both sides; the bend hides the lane beyond the oak; the grass verge opens beside the chaise; the field roofline appears beyond the hedge; the wheel tracks lead the eye toward the occupied verge.
grass_lane_rescue.crowd: three men struggle beside the chaise while two women sit inside
grass_lane_rescue.ambience: pony breathing, hedge insects, distant hoofbeats, women calling

barnet_crossing.described: The narrow sandy lane enters the main road through the centre of the picture. A tall clipped privet hedge fills the left edge and ends at the white gate of the red-brick corner house. The opposite villa wall holds the right edge. Beyond the opening, the main road runs across the frame with carts, horses, refugees, gas lamps, and a burning villa farther north. White dust hangs above the road and black smoke crosses the distant terrace. Summer sunlight falls from the east onto the hedge and road, while the villa fire adds red light at the far right. The lane gives the party a narrow approach to the traffic and the gate offers a fixed point beside the crush.
barnet_crossing.landmark: the white gate of the corner house
barnet_crossing.route: lane bend to the white gate and the main-road crossing
barnet_crossing.geometry: The left edge holds the privet hedge; the right edge holds the villa wall; the lane runs from foreground centre to the gate at medium size; the main road crosses the far half; the burning villa stands at the far-right edge; the white terrace sits beyond the road; gas lamps mark both road edges; dust fills the space between lane and traffic; the corner house anchors the gate; the road opens north and south beyond the lane mouth.
barnet_crossing.crowd: many refugees, carts, horses, and pedestrians stream north along the road
barnet_crossing.ambience: wheel clatter, hoofbeats, crowd cries, fire wind, splintering wood

hadley_water.described: The Hadley road runs from the lower left toward the far right beside a shallow gravelly brook. Pollard willows form a broken line along the right edge, and the muddy water margin occupies the lower-right quarter. Refugees kneel at the brook in the middle distance, with bundles and a shawl on the verge. Dust greys the hedges and village tower beyond. Afternoon sunlight falls from the west at frame left across the road and brook, making deep black shadows under the willows and along the far bank. The party's route follows the road toward the water, then continues east past the thirsty crowd and the willow trunks.
hadley_water.route: dusty road foreground to the brook beneath the willows
hadley_water.geometry: The lower left holds the road ruts; the lower right holds the brook margin; pollard willows line the right edge; kneeling refugees occupy medium size beside the far bank; the village tower rises at the far-left edge; bundles rest on the near verge; the road continues beyond the brook toward the eastern fields; muddy footprints mark the water edge; the willow trunks divide the road from the stream; the distant bank closes the route.
hadley_water.crowd: people kneel, drink, and push toward the brook
hadley_water.ambience: brook water, thirsty voices, carts, willow leaves, distant rail noise

east_barnet_night.described: The East Barnet field fills the foreground with a hedge and field gate along the lower edge. The railway cutting runs horizontally through the middle distance, with poles marching toward the right edge. Open fields and low hills occupy the far half beneath a cold evening sky. The halted chaise rests beside the hedge at the lower left, while fugitives pass along the road behind it. Evening sunlight falls from the west at the left edge across the field, leaving deep black shadows under the hedge and beside the gate. The field gives the party a stopping place between the road and the railway, with the distant line carrying the wider exodus beyond them.
east_barnet_night.route: halting hedge to the railway cutting at the far field
east_barnet_night.geometry: The hedge and gate occupy the lower edge; the chaise rests at lower left in medium size; the railway cutting crosses the middle distance; poles recede toward the far-right edge; hills meet the upper edge; the road runs behind the hedge; the field opens between the foreground gate and the distant rails; the field gate marks the stopping place; the railway line forms a dark horizontal band; the evening sky fills the upper third.
east_barnet_night.crowd: many fugitives pass the field and railway embankment toward the east
east_barnet_night.ambience: cold wind, railway clatter, pony breathing, distant footsteps

shots.frame: Wide over the river from the bank at morning: a stone bridge stands across the river with black smoke rising beyond it, and the water below it is jammed with barges and steamers packed with people.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in toward the bridge across the whole shot, travelling a hand's breadth; the crowded barges drift on the current; the black smoke rolls upward behind the towers.
shots.camera: on the stone river stairs at the height of a standing man, two hundred yards from the bridge, a 35mm lens. The morning sun comes from the RIGHT behind thin smoke and lays a pale sheen on the brown water
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS THE STONE BRIDGE: its two grey towers stand at the CENTRE of the TOP third with the high walkway between them. Black smoke rises behind it into the TOP edge. Barges crowded with people fill the river from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge across the BOTTOM third, and the wet stone stairs run across the BOTTOM edge. Coal smoke from the steamers drifts low across the water at the CENTRE, and wet bollards stand along the BOTTOM LEFT.
shots.crowd: people fighting savagely for standing-room in the carriages

sounds.sound: distant river shouts and steamer whistles

source: the stream of flight rising swiftly to a torrent, lashing in a foaming tumult round the railway stations
People were fighting savagely for standing-room in the carriages even at two o’clock
shots.turn: London's ordered life -> a city-wide flight
shots.why: The riverfront becomes part of the exodus, establishing a force larger than any single traveller.

shots.frame: Wide down the river beneath the stone bridge: steamers and barges lie side by side so close that people climb from deck to deck toward the shore.
shots.motion: The camera tracks sideways to the right along the wharf across the whole shot, travelling a hand's breadth; the steamer's funnel puffs smoke; people step from one deck to the next.
shots.camera: on a wharf platform above the water, fifty yards from the nearest steamer, a 35mm lens. The sun comes from the RIGHT and lights the funnels and the faces turned toward the shore
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS A PADDLE STEAMER at the CENTRE, its decks black with people and its funnel smoking. Barges crowd against it from the LEFT edge, the bridge arches stand across the TOP third, and the brown water shows in a narrow strip along the BOTTOM edge. Ropes hang from the steamer's rail at the LEFT third, and gulls wheel low over the water at the TOP RIGHT.
shots.crowd: people fighting savagely for standing-room in the carriages

sounds.sound: ropes striking wood and many voices calling

source: the stream of flight rising swiftly to a torrent, lashing in a foaming tumult round the railway stations
People were fighting savagely for standing-room in the carriages even at two o’clock
shots.turn: ordered river traffic -> crowded escape route
shots.why: The second view enlarges the hook from one bridge to the whole jammed river.

shots.frame: Medium on a constable at the foot of a wharf gate trying to hold back a pressing crowd with his arms spread, his helmet knocked crooked.
shots.motion: The camera tilts up to the helmet across the whole shot, travelling a hand's breadth; the crowd surges against his arms; his helmet slips further over one ear.
shots.camera: on the cobbles four paces from the constable at chest height, a 50mm lens. The light comes from the LEFT off the river and catches his silver helmet badge
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS THE CONSTABLE at the CENTRE, his dark blue tunic and crooked helmet in the brightest light, both arms out. Shoulders and hats of the crowd press in from the RIGHT edge, the iron wharf gate stands at the LEFT edge, and the river shows grey at the TOP third. Torn handbills lie on the wet cobbles at the BOTTOM edge, and a lamp post rises at the LEFT third behind the gate.

sounds.sound: ropes striking wood and many voices calling

source: By ten o’clock the police organisation, and by midday even the railway organisations, were losing coherency, losing shape and efficiency
shots.why: The escape route reaches the water and finds the same pressure there.

shots.frame: Insert on the river surface under the bridge as a low bank of black vapour rolls across the water toward the camera.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in toward THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS; the black vapour rolls forward over the water; the empty boat rocks and turns at the right edge.
shots.camera: at water level on a barge deck, ten yards from the vapour, a 35mm lens. Grey daylight comes from the TOP and the vapour swallows it
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS THE BANK OF BLACK VAPOUR at the CENTRE, low and heavy on the water. The underside of a bridge arch closes the TOP third, the brown water fills the BOTTOM third, and an empty rowing boat drifts at the RIGHT edge. Floating straw and a broken oar drift on the water at the BOTTOM RIGHT, and the arch's dark stone shows wet and dripping.
source: a cloud of slowly sinking black vapour drove along the Thames and across the flats of Lambeth, cutting off all escape over the bridges
shots.turn: bridges as exits -> bridges as barriers
shots.why: The chapter's escape question becomes physical: the city has routes, yet the vapour closes them.

shots.frame: Wide from a hill above the roads: every road out of the city is a dark moving line of people and carts heading north under a smoky sky.
shots.motion: The camera cranes up across the whole shot, travelling a hand's breadth; the dark lines on the roads move north; the smoke drifts across the sky.
shots.camera: on a hilltop pasture at the height of a standing man, a mile from the roads, a 35mm lens. The sun comes from the LEFT through haze and lights the dust over the roads
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS THE MAIN ROAD running from the BOTTOM edge up to the CENTRE, packed with a dark moving line of carts and people. Smaller roads join it from the LEFT edge and the RIGHT edge, rooftops fill the BOTTOM third, and smoke hangs across the TOP third. Hedgerows divide the fields at the BOTTOM third, and church spires rise above the rooftops at the LEFT third.
shots.crowd: a little island of survivors on Castle Hill
source: Another bank drove over Ealing, and surrounded a little island of survivors on Castle Hill, alive, but unable to escape
shots.why: The wider image carries the chapter's first escape failure to its full social scale.

shots.frame: Medium on the brother in a shop doorway at Chalk Farm, lifting a bicycle out through the broken glass of the window.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in on the brother across the whole shot, travelling a finger's breadth; he lifts the bicycle clear of the window frame; the front wheel spins as it comes free.
shots.camera: on the pavement three paces from him at chest height, a 50mm lens. Morning sun comes from the RIGHT down the street and lights his face and the bicycle frame
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS THE BROTHER at the CENTRE, both hands on the bicycle handlebars, the broken shop window behind him. Glass lies on the pavement at the BOTTOM edge, the empty street runs away at the RIGHT edge, and brick shopfronts close the LEFT edge. A brass shop bell hangs over the doorway at the TOP third, and a handcart lies tipped on its side at the RIGHT edge.

sounds.sound: plate glass breaking under the bicycle frame

source: my brother emerged upon the Chalk Farm road, dodged across through a hurrying swarm of vehicles, and had the luck to be foremost in the sack of a cycle shop
shots.why: The brother turns panic into movement by taking the first usable machine.

shots.frame: Insert on the front wheel of the bicycle on a dusty road at Edgware, the rim bent out of true, a man's boots beside it.
shots.motion: The camera tilts up to the front wheel across the whole shot, travelling a finger's breadth; the wheel turns once and stops against the buckle; dust lifts from the road.
shots.camera: at road level two paces from the wheel, a 50mm lens. Midday sun comes from the TOP LEFT and throws the spokes' shadow on the dust
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS THE BENT FRONT WHEEL at the CENTRE, its rim buckled. Dusty road fills the BOTTOM third, a man's brown boots stand at the RIGHT edge, and shopfronts show soft along the TOP third. A dropped bundle tied with string lies in the dust at the LEFT edge, and the chain hangs loose from the sprocket.
source: A mile from Edgware the rim of the wheel broke, and the machine became unridable
shots.turn: bicycle as freedom -> bicycle as burden
shots.why: The failed machine forces the brother back onto his own strength and into the growing refugee stream.

shots.frame: Medium on the brother at the counter of an abandoned inn at Edgware, eating bread from a plate with his bandaged hand.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in toward THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS; the brother tears the bread and eats; he turns his head toward the doorway.
shots.camera: inside the inn doorway three paces from him at chest height, a 50mm lens. Daylight comes from the LEFT through the doorway onto his face and the bread
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS THE BROTHER at the CENTRE, bread in his hand, the bare wooden counter in front of him. The open doorway and the bright road show at the LEFT edge, empty shelves stand along the RIGHT edge, and the plate sits on the counter at the BOTTOM third. A cold teapot and two cups stand at the RIGHT third of the counter, and sunlight falls in a bright bar across the floor.
source: He succeeded in getting some food at an inn
The flying people increased in number
At that time the road was crowded, but as yet far from congested.
shots.why: Food gives the brother a short reserve before the growing flight draws him onward.

shots.frame: Wide down a green lane past Barnet: the brother vaults a stile toward a pony-chaise at the far bend, where two men struggle with the women at the wheels and a third holds the pony's head.
shots.motion: The camera pans to the right with the brother across the whole shot, travelling a hand's breadth; he drops from the stile and runs toward the chaise; the pony throws its head.
shots.camera: at the stile at the height of a standing man, thirty yards from the chaise, a 35mm lens. Morning sun comes from the RIGHT through the hedge tops in bright bands across the ruts
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS THE BROTHER at the LEFT third, one leg over the wooden stile. The pony-chaise stands small at the far bend at the CENTRE with two women in it and three men at its wheels. Hawthorn hedges close both the LEFT edge and the RIGHT edge, and the dusty ruts run from the BOTTOM edge to the chaise. Wild roses cover the hedge at the TOP LEFT, and a fingerpost leans beside the stile at the BOTTOM LEFT.

sounds.sound: three men shouting and striking the pony-chaise

source: a couple of men struggling to drag them out of the little pony-chaise
a third with difficulty held the frightened pony’s head
shots.why: The brother finds a danger that demands a choice, and the women become the people he will carry onward.

shots.frame: Medium on the brother beside the chaise wheel driving a robber in a black reefer jacket back against the hedge with his fists.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in toward the right with the struggle across; the brother drives the robber back into the hedge; the robber's bowler falls.
shots.camera: in the lane four paces from the fight at chest height, a 50mm lens. Sun comes from the RIGHT through the hedge and lights the brother's face and raised fist
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS THE BROTHER at the CENTRE, his fist raised, his torn cuff and bandaged wrist in the light. The robber in a black reefer jacket stumbles back at the RIGHT edge, the chaise wheel fills the LEFT edge, and the hawthorn hedge closes the TOP third. The pony's harness shines at the TOP LEFT, and trampled dog-roses lie in the grass at the BOTTOM edge.

sounds.sound: a body striking the wooden chaise wheel

source: my brother, realising from his antagonist’s face that a fight was unavoidable, and being an expert boxer, went into him forthwith and sent him down against the wheel of the chaise
shots.turn: threat surrounds the women -> threat loses one attacker
shots.why: The brother's physical skill changes the balance, while the narrow lane keeps danger close.

shots.frame: Close on Miss Elphinstone in the chaise seat, a black revolver held out level in her hand, her face set.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in on Miss Elphinstone across the whole shot, travelling a finger's breadth; she raises the revolver; her finger tightens on the trigger as she speaks.
shots.camera: beside the chaise at her shoulder height, one pace away, an 85mm lens. Sun comes from the LEFT and lights her face and the barrel of the revolver
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS MISS ELPHINSTONE'S FACE at the CENTRE, her head half the frame's height, her eyes along the barrel. The revolver crosses the RIGHT third, the red-lined seat shows at the BOTTOM edge, and green hedge fills the LEFT edge and the TOP edge. A strand of her dark hair has come loose at her temple, and her other hand grips the seat rail at the BOTTOM LEFT.
source: “Take this!” said the slender lady, and she gave my brother her revolver
shots.turn: rescued women as dependants -> rescued women as partners
shots.why: The woman gives the brother a weapon and shares the responsibility for their escape.

shots.frame: Medium close on Miss Elphinstone and the brother side by side on the chaise seat as she hands him the reins and the chaise starts down the lane.
shots.motion: The camera pulls back ahead of the chaise across the whole shot, travelling a hand's breadth; Miss Elphinstone passes the reins to the brother; the chaise rolls forward.
shots.camera: on the lane in front of the pony at seat height, two paces away, a 50mm lens. Sun comes from the RIGHT and lights both faces
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS MISS ELPHINSTONE at the LEFT third, her head a third of the frame's height, the reins in her hand. The brother sits at the RIGHT third reaching for the reins, the red-lined seat runs across the BOTTOM edge, and the hedge-lined lane runs away behind them across the TOP third. The pony's ears show at the BOTTOM CENTRE, and dust rises from the wheels into the light at the LEFT edge.
source: “I’ll sit here,” said my brother, “if I may”
“Give me the reins,” she said, and laid the whip along the pony’s side

She explained that they had as much as thirty pounds in gold, besides a five-pound note, and suggested that with that they might get upon a train at St. Albans or New Barnet. My brother thought that was hopeless, seeing the fury of the Londoners to crowd upon the trains, and broached his own idea of striking across Essex towards Harwich and thence escaping from the country altogether.
shots.why: The brother joins the chaise, and the woman takes command of the pony.

shots.frame: Wide from the hill above Barnet: the great north road below is one solid torrent of carts, cabs and people, with villas burning beyond it under rolling smoke.
shots.motion: The camera cranes up over the torrent across the whole shot, travelling a hand's breadth; the torrent on the road flows on; flames lift above the villa roofs.
shots.camera: at the top of the lane where it meets the hill, at the height of a standing man, two hundred yards from the road, a 35mm lens. The sun comes from the RIGHT through the smoke in a hot orange haze
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS THE TORRENT ON THE MAIN ROAD running across the CENTRE from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge. Burning villas send smoke into the TOP third, the green slope of the lane fills the BOTTOM third, and a small pony-chaise stands at the BOTTOM LEFT where the lane drops to the road. A church tower stands dark against the smoke at the TOP RIGHT, and a broken fence runs down the slope at the BOTTOM RIGHT.

sounds.sound: distant wheels, hooves, and burning timber

source: Then round the corner of the lane, from between the villas that guarded it at its confluence with the high road, came a little cart drawn by a sweating black pony and driven by a sallow youth in a bowler hat, grey with dust.
For the main road was a boiling stream of people, a torrent of human beings rushing northward, one pressing on another.
shots.why: The route ahead changes from refuge into a visible mass flight.

shots.frame: Medium close on Mrs. Elphinstone in the back of the chaise, clutching her white skirt and staring at the road ahead.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in on Mrs. Elphinstone across the whole shot, travelling a finger's breadth; she grips her skirt tighter; she turns her head toward the road as she speaks.
shots.camera: beside the chaise at her eye level, two paces away, a 50mm lens. The orange light of the fires comes from the RIGHT onto her face and her white dress
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS MRS. ELPHINSTONE'S FACE at the CENTRE, her head a third of the frame's height, her mouth open. Her hands rest in her lap at the BOTTOM third, the black chaise hood rises behind her at the LEFT edge, and grey smoke fills the TOP RIGHT. Her straw hat sits askew on her hair, and the chaise's iron step shows at the BOTTOM LEFT.

sounds.sound: refugees crying and wheels striking the road

source: “Good heavens!” cried Mrs. Elphinstone. “What is this you are driving us into?”
shots.why: Mrs. Elphinstone voices the question the picture has already posed.

shots.frame: Medium on the brother at the hedge by the road, lifting a fallen child from the dust as carts roll past behind him.
shots.motion: The camera orbits to the left around the brother across the whole shot, travelling a hand's breadth; the brother lifts the child out of the dust; a cart wheel rolls past behind him.
shots.camera: on the verge four paces from him at waist height, a 50mm lens. Hazy sun comes from the LEFT and lights his back and the child
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS THE BROTHER at the CENTRE, bent over the small child in the dust. The tall hedge closes the LEFT edge, a cart wheel and a horse's legs pass at the RIGHT edge, and dust hangs across the TOP third. A child's dropped cap lies in the dust at the BOTTOM RIGHT, and the hedge leaves are grey with dust at the LEFT edge.
source: a little girl of eight or nine … threw herself under the hedge close by my brother, weeping
shots.turn: crowd as spectacle -> child as immediate duty
shots.why: The brother's attention leaves the large disaster and settles on one child within reach.

shots.frame: Medium close on the brother crouched at the roadside beside Lord Garrick on his stretcher, speaking anxiously to him over the noise of the road.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in on the brother across the whole shot, travelling a finger's breadth; he leans toward the stretcher as he speaks; Lord Garrick lifts one hand from the blanket.
shots.camera: at crouching height on the verge, two paces from them, a 50mm lens. Hazy light comes from the RIGHT and lights the brother's face and the claret dressing gown
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS THE BROTHER'S FACE at the RIGHT third, his head a third of the frame's height, turned toward the stretcher. Lord Garrick lies on the stretcher at the LEFT third in his claret dressing gown, the stretcher poles run along the BOTTOM edge, and dusty road with passing wheels fills the TOP third. A blanket lies over Lord Garrick's knees at the BOTTOM LEFT, and the brother's bandaged wrist rests on his knee at the RIGHT third.

sounds.sound: carriage wheels striking the dusty road

source: two men lifted out something on a white stretcher and put it gently on the grass beneath the privet hedge
He is dying fast, and very thirsty. It is Lord Garrick.
shots.why: The dying judge reveals that even public rank has become helpless inside the flight.

shots.frame: Insert on the road at hoof level: gold sovereigns scattered in the dust under a horse's hooves and a cart wheel, a man's hand reaching for them.
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame; the hand reaches toward the coins; the cart wheel rolls past the coins in the dust.
shots.camera: at road level one pace from the coins, a 50mm lens. Dusty sun comes from the TOP LEFT and glints on the gold
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS THE SCATTERED SOVEREIGNS at the CENTRE, bright in the dust. A horse's hooves stamp at the TOP third, a cart wheel turns at the RIGHT edge, and a man's hand reaches in from the LEFT edge. Hoof prints and wheel ruts score the dust at the BOTTOM edge, and a dropped purse lies open at the RIGHT third.

sounds.sound: horse hooves striking beside the fallen man

source: a bearded, eagle-faced man lugging a small handbag, which split even as my brother’s eyes rested on it and disgorged a mass of sovereigns
the wheel had broken his back
shots.why: The brother reaches the fallen man, yet the moving road defeats the rescue and carries the decision onward.

shots.frame: Medium on the brother at the pony's head, turning the frightened animal back toward the lane while the traffic presses past.
shots.motion: The camera holds a locked-off frame; he turns the pony's head back toward the lane; the pony tosses its mane.
shots.camera: on the road four paces from him at chest height, a 50mm lens. Hazy sun comes from the RIGHT and lights his face and the pony's blaze
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS THE BROTHER at the CENTRE, his hand at the pony's head. The pony's head fills the LEFT third, the black chaise stands behind him at the RIGHT third, and carts and dust pass across the TOP third. The pony's blinkers and brass harness catch the light at the LEFT third, and dust drifts across the road at the TOP RIGHT.
source: “Let us go back!” he shouted, and began turning the pony round
they went back a hundred yards the way they had come
shots.why: The crush forces the brother to retreat, placing the women and the road's danger on opposite sides.

shots.frame: Medium close on the brother standing at the chaise and Miss Elphinstone on its seat, pointing across the road toward a gap in the traffic.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in on the brother across the whole shot, travelling a finger's breadth; the brother points across the road; Miss Elphinstone turns her head to look.
shots.camera: on the road at the chaise's step at chest height, two paces away, a 50mm lens. Hazy sun comes from the LEFT and lights both faces
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS THE BROTHER at the LEFT third, his head a third of the frame's height, his arm pointing to the RIGHT. Miss Elphinstone sits on the chaise seat at the RIGHT third, the black chaise fills the BOTTOM RIGHT, and the road and dust fill the TOP third. The chaise's lamp hangs at the RIGHT edge, and the brother's bandaged wrist shows at the BOTTOM LEFT.

sounds.sound: waggon wheels locking against chaise wheels

source: my brother plunged into the traffic and held back a cab horse, while she drove the pony across its head
A waggon locked wheels for a moment and ripped a long splinter from the chaise
shots.turn: retreat -> shared decision to enter the torrent
shots.why: The brother and Miss Elphinstone act together, forcing the chaise into the current and taking shared control.

shots.frame: Wide over the brook at Hadley: the chaise stands on the road beyond the willows while refugees kneel at the water to drink.
shots.motion: The camera tracks sideways to the right along the bank across the whole shot, travelling a hand's breadth; the refugees cup water to their mouths; the pony lowers its head toward the brook.
shots.camera: on the far bank of the brook at the height of a standing man, thirty yards from the chaise, a 35mm lens. Afternoon sun comes from the LEFT through the willows and glints on the water
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS THE SHALLOW BROOK running from the BOTTOM edge to the CENTRE, with refugees kneeling at its edge. The black pony-chaise stands small on the road at the LEFT third, pollard willows line the RIGHT edge, and the church tower rises at the TOP LEFT. A dropped bundle lies on the bank at the BOTTOM RIGHT, and willow leaves trail into the water at the RIGHT third.
shots.crowd: people kneel, drink, and push toward the brook

sounds.sound: people shouting and splashing at the brook

source: they came upon a great multitude of people drinking at the stream, some fighting to come at the water
shots.why: The road carries them east, but thirst shows that escape has not become safety.

shots.frame: Insert on two trains passing one after the other through a cutting at dusk, their carriage roofs crowded with people.
shots.motion: The camera pans to the left with the trains across the whole shot, travelling a hand's breadth; the engines drive forward; smoke streams back over the crowded roofs.
shots.camera: on the embankment above the cutting at the height of a standing man, twenty yards from the line, a 35mm lens. The last sunset light comes from the LEFT and lights the smoke
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS THE NEAREST ENGINE at the CENTRE, smoke pouring from its funnel. The second train runs along the RIGHT edge, the rails fill the BOTTOM third, and the evening sky fills the TOP third. Grass grows along the cutting at the BOTTOM LEFT, and smoke trails behind the engines across the TOP RIGHT.
shots.crowd: crowds packed on the carriage roofs

sounds.sound: two trains clattering along the rails

source: they saw two trains running slowly one after the other without signal or order—trains swarming with people
shots.why: The railway offers motion without order, mirroring the road and widening the chapter's social collapse.

shots.frame: Medium on the brother standing by the halted chaise in a field near East Barnet at dusk, looking back down the road.
shots.motion: The camera pulls back from the brother to the chaise across the whole shot, travelling a hand's breadth; he turns his head to look back down the road; the pony shifts its weight behind him.
shots.camera: on the grass verge four paces from him at chest height, a 50mm lens. The last light comes from the LEFT and edges his face and shoulder
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS THE BROTHER at the CENTRE, standing still with his bandaged hand at his side. The chaise stands at the LEFT third, the wooden gate closes the RIGHT edge, and the darkening sky fills the TOP third. The pony stands with lowered head behind the chaise at the LEFT edge, and the road runs pale into the dusk at the RIGHT third.
source: Near this place they halted for the rest of the afternoon
shots.why: The party reaches a place where exhaustion briefly interrupts the journey.

shots.frame: Medium close on the brother and Miss Elphinstone standing beside the halted chaise in the cold dusk, he keeping watch beside her.
shots.motion: The camera cranes up across the whole shot, travelling a finger's breadth; the brother keeps his eyes on the road; Miss Elphinstone draws her coat tighter against the cold.
shots.camera: on the verge at the chaise step at chest height, two paces away, a 50mm lens. The last light comes from the LEFT and edges both faces
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS MISS ELPHINSTONE at the LEFT third, her head a third of the frame's height, standing beside the chaise. The brother stands at the RIGHT third, his head a third of the frame's height, watching the road, and the dusk sky fills the TOP third. The chaise's dark hood rises behind her at the LEFT edge, and the field gate shows dim beyond him at the RIGHT edge.
source: They began to suffer the beginnings of hunger; the night was cold, and none of them dared to sleep
shots.why: The party gains shelter beside the route, yet hunger and cold keep the journey alive inside them.

shots.frame: Insert on the road beside the hedge at evening as a few fugitives walk past into the dark.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in toward THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS; the walkers move along the road toward the dark; a lantern swings in one walker's hand.
shots.camera: at the gate post at waist height, ten yards from the road, a 35mm lens. Deep blue dusk light comes from the TOP and the walkers are dark shapes against it
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS THE PALE ROAD running from the BOTTOM edge to the CENTRE. The hedge fills the LEFT edge, walkers pass small at the CENTRE, and the deep blue sky fills the TOP third. Hedges line both sides of the road at the LEFT and RIGHT thirds, and a lantern glows small among the walkers at the CENTRE.
shots.crowd: a few distant walkers on the road
source: in the evening many people came hurrying along the road nearby their stopping place, fleeing from unknown dangers before them
shots.turn: halted party -> road still carrying danger
shots.why: The evening road proves that the exodus continues beyond the party's temporary halt.

shots.frame: Insert on the dark field beyond the hedge under the first stars, the road and passing fugitives beyond the chaise.
shots.motion: The camera cranes up across the whole shot, travelling a finger's breadth; the grass stirs in the night wind; the pony shifts beside the chaise.
shots.camera: low in the grass at knee height, twenty yards from the chaise, a 35mm lens. Starlight and the last glow come from the RIGHT along the horizon
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS THE CHAise at the CENTRE beside the hedge. Dark grass fills the BOTTOM third, the hedge stands at the LEFT edge, and the first stars show across the TOP third. The pony stands dark beside the chaise at the RIGHT third, and the road runs pale along the BOTTOM RIGHT toward the gate. A thin mist lies over the grass at the CENTRE, and the black hedge line closes the far horizon.
shots.crowd: a few fugitives pass along the road beyond the hedge
source: the night was cold, and none of them dared to sleep
shots.why: A held beat lets the cost of the crossing register before the world's answer arrives.

shots.frame: Medium on the brother and Miss Elphinstone standing awake beside the chaise in the cold night, he standing guard beside her.
shots.motion: The camera pulls back from the chaise across the whole shot, travelling a hand's breadth; the brother looks out at the dark road; Miss Elphinstone pulls her shawl around her shoulders.
shots.camera: on the verge four paces from them at chest height, a 50mm lens. Faint starlight comes from the RIGHT and edges both faces
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS THE BROTHER at the RIGHT third, standing, his bandaged hand at his side. Miss Elphinstone stands at the LEFT third beside the black chaise, the black chaise fills the LEFT edge, and the dark road runs away across the TOP third. Starlight edges the chaise's iron wheel at the BOTTOM LEFT, and the dark field gate stands at the RIGHT edge.
source: Near this place they halted for the rest of the afternoon
the night was cold, and none of them dared to sleep
in the evening many people came hurrying along the road nearby their stopping place
shots.turn: temporary halt -> exodus continues around them
shots.why: The world answers the question with continued flight: the party survives the crossing, yet the road keeps moving around them.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I watch London turn its streets into one northward flight beneath the bridges.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The river crowds beneath the bridge, and the city presses toward every remaining road.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The police lose coherence, then railway order follows; stations become traps for the fleeing crowd.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Black vapour crosses the Thames and closes the bridges.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Across England, survivors find each road narrowed by the same advancing disaster.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The brother escapes the railway crush, takes a bicycle, and rides beyond the broken route.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The wheel fails at Edgware, and the brother leaves the machine for the village.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Food steadies him briefly; then fugitives gather while news stays distant.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Beyond the stile, I find the brother beside screams and a trapped chaise.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The brother drives the attackers from the chaise.

lines.speaker: miss_elphinstone
lines.text: Take this!

lines.speaker: miss_elphinstone
lines.text: Give me the reins.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The chaise leaves the lane with the brother and women.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Smoke and flame rise beyond the villas; the quiet lane meets a moving catastrophe.

lines.speaker: mrs_elphinstone
lines.text: Good heavens! What is this you are driving us into?

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The road becomes a human torrent, and one child falls beside the hedge.

lines.speaker: narrators_brother
lines.text: There may be a tap. We have no water. I dare not leave my people.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Coins scatter; the brother reaches into a deadly crush.

lines.speaker: narrators_brother
lines.text: We must go that way.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Past Barnet, thirst gathers fugitives at the brook, where water becomes another struggle.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Two trains carry the same disorder north, their crowded roofs crossing the evening fields.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The party halts near East Barnet, while the day's violence leaves the road around them.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Hunger and cold enter the halt; the brother keeps watch beside the women.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Evening fugitives pass, extending the flight into darkness.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Fugitives pass; the three stay awake in cold.
